facts.quote: These rules apply to confirmed night-time reservations on shared instruments.
Transfer a reservation only after the receiving observer accepts it and the duty operator approves the transfer.
Retain the original reservation identifier and record both observers in the audit trail.

queries.question: When should wind stop observations, what is required to restart, and may an indoor instrument continue?

facts.quote: Weather decisions govern execution, not ownership of reservations.
Suspend outdoor observations when the wind interlock opens.
Resume only after the interlock closes and the duty operator records a restart approval.
An instrument explicitly classified as indoor may continue during a wind suspension, provided its own safety interlocks remain closed.
A roof visible as closed on the calendar does not establish indoor classification.

queries.question: What must the gateway do after excessive clock drift, including recovery when the reference clock is unavailable?

facts.quote: The gateway compares instrument time with the observatory reference before executing a schedule.
If the absolute clock offset exceeds two seconds, pause schedule execution and notify the duty operator.
Resume only after two consecutive reference checks report an offset within two seconds.
If the reference clock is unavailable, keep execution paused; a local clock reading alone cannot satisfy either recovery check.
